title: Use an instance method reference on a specific object `System.out::println` for `forEach`.
shortTitle: Use an instance method reference on a specific object System.out::println for forEach
keyPoints: System.out::println is a bound instance-method reference: the receiver (System.out) is fixed at creation time
It serves as a Consumer<T>, printing each element passed by forEach
Bound references capture a specific object; unbound references (String::length) supply the receiver at call time
System.out::println is fine for debugging but not for production logging
In production, use a Logger reference like logger::info as the Consumer
The bound form captures the receiver once and reuses it for every element

s1_definition.oneliner: System.out::println is a bound reference: the receiver is the specific System.out object, so forEach prints each element.
s1_definition.profdef:
- A **bound instance-method reference** `instance::method` captures a specific receiver object.
- **System.out::println** captures the `System.out` PrintStream as the receiver.
- It serves as `Consumer<T>`: forEach(System.out::println) prints every element.
- **Bound** = receiver is fixed. **Unbound** (String::length) = receiver is supplied per call.
- Fine for debugging; use a proper Logger in production.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India has one specific printer at her desk. Rather than saying 'take an item and send it to this printer', she just points at the printer's print action. Every item goes to that same printer.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Bound reference: System.out::println

  Capture:
    receiver = System.out  (fixed at creation)

  forEach call:
    element "Rajesh" → System.out.println("Rajesh")
    element "Priya"  → System.out.println("Priya")
    element "Amit"   → System.out.println("Amit")

  Compare with unbound (String::length):
    element "Rajesh" → "Rajesh".length()  (element IS the receiver)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A bound instance-method reference fixes the receiver at the moment the reference is created. System.out::println captures the System.out PrintStream, so forEach passes each element to that specific object's println method, printing every element on its own line.

The distinction is bound vs unbound: in the bound form the receiver is already chosen and only the method argument comes from the stream. In the unbound form (like String::length), the stream element itself becomes the receiver.

System.out::println is perfect for quick debugging but wrong for production. At the National Bank of India, production code uses a Logger bound reference like log::info instead. The concept is the same: fix the receiver, feed it elements.

Remember one sentence: System.out::println is a bound reference with a fixed receiver, fine for debugging but replaced by a Logger reference in production.
